answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and places that color's Player ID card upright in its plastic stand, visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting-card set with their color on the backs; remove cards targeting colors not in play and keep their own Ambush card. Put the Gold Bar deck face down beside the play area and deal four cards face down into the center, with values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: “upright in their plastic stand”; “Remove cards targeting colors that are not playing”; “Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.”

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player turn order; voting is simultaneous. Each player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed” and “reveal all choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is needed. Red is the sole Target because Red received the most votes (three); the Target is whoever receives the most votes, regardless of whether that is a majority of all votes.
answers.evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target.”

answers.answer: Both Red and Blue are Targets because they are tied for the most votes. With neither protected by a successful Ambush, both are eliminated as Targets. A player may satisfy the voting requirement for survival by voting for either tied Target.
answers.evidence: Vote: “If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets”; “With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.”

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the sole Target, and receiving no votes does not protect a player. The rule eliminates every other player who did not vote for any Target, subject to the successful-Ambush exception; Green did not Ambush.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated, subject to the successful Ambush exception below.”

answers.answer: Ambush cards do not count as votes, so the counted votes are Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow. Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and both are Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds; Red survives and may eliminate Yellow, the player who voted for Red. Yellow is eliminated, and Pink survives because Pink voted for tied Target Yellow. Red and Pink remain for a Final Showdown.
answers.evidence: Ambush example: “Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and are both Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives ... Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives.”

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambush lets its player choose exactly one player who voted for them to eliminate. They cannot eliminate all four voters and cannot choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “chooses one of the players who voted for them”; “cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.”

answers.answer: That player eliminates themselves. An Ambush only works if its player is a Target in that vote.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, the round continues with another conspiracy and vote among the surviving players only.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure table: “Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.”

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points: each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points, so the total points depend on the cards' values.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “One | That survivor collects all four central Gold Bars.” Components: “receiving one bar means receiving one card whose value is 3, 4, or 5 points.”

answers.answer: The two survivors resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of three cards—Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go—then may discuss intentions and a bargain. Each chooses one card, places it face down, and, when both are ready, they reveal simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go”; each “chooses one ... card and places it face down”; reveal “simultaneously.”

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for the no-survivor result, including those eliminated in that vote. Leave the four central bars for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.”

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share/Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”

answers.answer: The finalist choosing Share gets zero central bars; the finalist choosing Steal gets all four central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share against Steal: “You get 0; opponent gets 4.”

answers.answer: The finalist choosing Grab One & Go gets one central bar, and the finalist choosing Steal gets the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table: Grab One & Go against Steal gives “You get 1; opponent gets 3”; the note says Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.

answers.answer: The finalist choosing Grab One & Go gets one central bar, and the finalist choosing Share gets the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table: Share against Grab One & Go gives “You get 3; opponent gets 1”; the note says Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar. Two bars remain in the center. If play continues, add two new bars to bring the central pool to four.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “each receives one and the other two bars remain central”; “add just two new bars for the next round.”

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every player other than the two finalists receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “neither finalist receives gold”; “give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck”; “Leave all four central bars for the next round.”

answers.answer: Victory is checked at the end of the round, after Gold Bars are awarded. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players, it is at least 24. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring: “at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded”; thresholds are “at least 25” for 6–9 and “at least 24” for 10–12; “the highest point total wins.”

answers.answer: For exactly two tied qualifying leaders, the tied players conduct another Final Showdown. Showdowns are repeated as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total; one extra Showdown does not end the tie if the highest totals remain tied. The summary does not specify how to supply the central pot for these extra game-end Showdowns. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns for the next round, including players eliminated earlier in the round; stand all Player ID cards upright.
answers.evidence: Scoring: tied highest qualifying totals “conduct another Final Showdown” and “Repeat these Showdowns as necessary”; the summary also says the booklet does not “specify how to supply the pot for extra game-end tie Showdowns.” Turn Structure: “If there is no winner, everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright.”

answers.answer: Before each vote, players conspire for roughly a minute and a half at most. They may communicate by any method, openly or secretly, including texting or showing a Voting card. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
answers.evidence: Conspire: “for roughly a minute and a half at most”; any method is allowed, including “texting” and “showing a Voting card”; “the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.”

answers.answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the target's visible ID color and place it face down in front of yourself. If you want to defend yourself against being targeted, play your own Ambush card instead.
answers.evidence: Vote: “To target someone, use the card matching that player's visible ID color”; each player places one card “face down in front of themselves”; “To defend yourself ... play your Ambush card instead.”

answers.answer: Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; they are the players eligible to participate in the next vote of that round.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.”

answers.answer: Because all four central bars were awarded, deal four new Gold Bar cards face down, keeping their values hidden, to prepare the next central pool. If nobody wins the game, this is the new round's four-card pool.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “If the entire pot was awarded, deal four new hidden-value bars”; the central pool is dealt face down with values hidden.

answers.answer: Yes. Blue and Purple are both Targets because four and three are tied for the most votes among those seven counted votes; Blue's successful Ambush does not remove Purple's Target status. Voters for Purple satisfy the voting requirement by voting for a tied Target and may survive, unless otherwise eliminated by a rule such as a successful retaliation. Blue's retaliation is restricted to someone who voted for Blue, so it cannot choose a voter for Purple who did not also vote for Blue.
answers.evidence: Vote: all players tied for most votes “are Targets”; “With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.” Ambush: it “does not prevent another player from being a tied Target” and retaliation chooses one who voted for the ambusher.

answers.answer: The booklet's stated instruction is that tied highest qualifying totals conduct another Final Showdown and repeat as necessary until one player at the table has the highest total. However, it does not specify how to arrange a Showdown with three or more tied players; the multiway procedure is unsupported by the summary and requires publisher clarification.
answers.evidence: Scoring says tied leaders “conduct another Final Showdown,” but explicitly states: “It provides no arrangement for three or more players tied for the highest qualifying total.”

answers.answer: Yes. In an extra Showdown where both tied players Steal, each player outside that pair receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. The outside player's points could make them the single highest-scoring winner; the summary says this can happen.
answers.evidence: Scoring: “The one-bar deck reward for everyone outside a double-Steal pair can therefore make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner.”
